licenses.issuingAuthority: Pollution Control Board, Assam — approval by the Member Secretary / Chief Environmental Engineer, as per delegation

portal.name: Assam Single Window (EODB) Pollution portal, also accessible via the Sewa Setu State Portal under the Assam Right to Public Services (ARTPS) Act; back-end processing through OCMMS / the CPCB Consent Management System

timeline.basis: ARTPS Act notified timelines, slabbed by pollution category: Green 30 working days, Orange 40, Red non-EIA (no TAC) 70, Red EIA projects with TAC 100, Red projects covered under the EIA Notification 2006 120 working days. The Board's own Guidelines separately state CTE/CTO must be processed within 120 days overall.
timeline.text: Timeline depends on the self-determined pollution category: 30 working days for Green up to 120 working days for Red category projects covered under the EIA Notification, 2006. A deficiency query restarts the clock, since the application is treated as made only from the date the clarification is received.

documents: Land documents – sale deed, jamabandi, trace map, non-encumbrance certificate and revenue clearance certificate (or rent/lease deed; or allotment letter of the designated authority if inside a notified industrial area/estate)
Project report containing the detailed Environment Management Plan
Site plan prepared by a competent engineer

Layout plan showing units/stack/chimney/emission points, drainage and final disposal of liquid effluent, solid waste collection/storage/disposal facility, and demarcation of open area and green belt with dimensions
NOC from the local authority (urban/rural local body)
Non-agricultural land certificate from the Circle Officer, if the land is classified as agricultural (specifically insisted upon for brick kilns and stone crushers)
Copy of Memorandum & Articles of Association / partnership deed / power of attorney (except proprietorship firms)
Estimated project cost on land, building, plant and machinery certified by a CA, or an affidavit/undertaking on Rs. 10 non-judicial stamp paper, duly notarised
Registration certificate of DI&CC (District Industries & Commerce Centre)
Proof of online payment of the consent fee in favour of the Member Secretary, PCB Assam, as per the latest fee notification
Environmental Clearance (EC) from MoEF&CC / SEIAA, if the project attracts the EIA Notification, 2006
Affidavit undertaking to abide by the Board's terms and conditions and to install the pollution control devices in the EMP before commissioning
licenses.documentsNote: CTE extension / auto-renewal additionally requires: requisition letter seeking extension; copy of the valid CTE and EC order (if applicable); progress report of construction and installation of pollution control systems with photographs; reasons for the extension and the estimated time required; and latitude/longitude of the project site.

deemedApproval.text: There is no operational deemed-approval mechanism for CTE in Assam. The ARTPS Act provides a first and second appeal with compensatory cost against delay, but not automatic grant of the service.

validity.text: Standard validity is 5 years for Red, Orange and Green category CTE. Extension is granted for a maximum of 5 years at a time, restricted to the validity of the Environmental Clearance for EIA-covered projects. If the unit is not commissioned and no extension is sought within the validity period, a fresh CTE application is required.

fees.text: Application form fee of Rs. 100 (over and above the consent fee), plus a CTE (NOC) consent fee based on capital-investment slab, ranging from Rs. 2,000 (up to Rs. 5 lakh) to Rs. 7,00,000 (above Rs. 200 crore). Fee is linked to capital investment on land, building, plant and machinery, not to pollution load; CTE carries a single fee (unlike CTO, which has separate Water Act and Air Act fees).

steps.title: Self-determine pollution category (Red/Orange/Green/White per CPCB Pollution Index)
steps.note: White category units are exempt from the consent requirement.

steps.title: Register on Assam Single Window (EODB) Pollution portal / Sewa Setu
File application online, upload checklist documents, pay application form fee (Rs. 100) plus consent fee
System-generated acknowledgement with reference number; SMS/e-mail alert; forwarded to Regional Office
Regional Office scrutinises for completeness; deficiency query gives 20 days to respond
steps.note: Timeline clock restarts from the date the clarification is received.

steps.title: Site inspection by Regional Office inspectors
steps.note: Green category industries are exempt from inspection.

steps.title: RO recommendation forwarded to Zonal/Head Office; Red/EIA cases additionally go to TAC or the Consent Committee
Approval by competent authority; order prepared within 5 working days of marking, uploaded within 2 working days of issue
CTE granted — standard validity 5 years for Red, Orange and Green categories

ed.location: Pollution Control Board, Assam (Head Office), Bamunimaidan, Guwahati, Assam

remarks: Quantitative inputs still to be obtained from the Board for the CoR computation: number of CTE and CTO applications received, disposed and pending by category for required financial years under the COR study.

findings.text: Two separate consents (CTE then CTO) are required for the same unit with a substantially overlapping document set — land documents, site plan, layout plan, process flow, raw material list, project report, constitution documents and pollution control device details are called for at both stages.
Separate consent fees and effectively separate processing apply under the Water Act and the Air Act for the same unit, same premises, same inspection and same order.

Consent fee is structured on total capital investment rather than pollution load, so a capital-intensive but low-polluting Green unit above Rs. 200 crore pays Rs. 7,00,000 for CTE while a smaller but heavily polluting unit pays a fraction.
A financial certificate or notarised affidavit on investment is required at CTE, again at CTO, and a CA-certified balance sheet again at every renewal/auto-renewal.
A deficiency query gives 20 days for the applicant to respond, and the application is treated as made only from the date the clarification is received, restarting the statutory timeline clock.

Site inspection is described as the single largest contributor to elapsed time in CTO-linked cases, since inspection dates depend on Regional Office staff availability and sampling/analysis turnaround.
Green category industries are exempt from physical inspection, converting their process into a desk appraisal, while White category units are exempt from the consent requirement altogether.

The process is completely online for submission, payment, tracking and download but not fully paperless: site inspection, laboratory sampling, the bank guarantee instrument, notarised affidavits and dispatch of the signed order by Speed Post all remain physical.
There is no operational deemed-approval mechanism for CTE; the ARTPS Act gives only a first and second appeal with compensatory cost for delay, not automatic grant of the service.

Suggested reform: an integrated/common consent application with a single document repository, and for Green/Orange non-EIA units a combined CTE-cum-CTO issued at CTE stage, estimated to save one full 30–40 working day cycle.

Suggested reform: system-scheduled inspection within 15 working days of a complete application with auto-escalation on lapse, and acceptance of NABL-accredited third-party test reports, estimated to save 20–30 working days in a typical Red non-EIA case.

Suggested reform: an OCMMS-generated digitally signed provisional consent auto-issued for Green/Orange non-EIA cases on lapse of the notified ARTPS timeline, valid for one year subject to post-facto verification and revocation.

Recommended elimination of documents the Government already holds — DI&CC registration, local authority NOC, non-agricultural land certificate, jamabandi/trace map/non-encumbrance/revenue clearance — via API-based verification and a single applicant document locker.

Auto-renewal of both CTE and CTO on self-certification was introduced by notifications dated 15.09.2025, with internal disposal timelines of 5 working days at the Regional Office and 3 working days at the Zonal/Head Office.

PCB Guidelines require the consent order to be uploaded on the OCMMS portal within 2 working days of issue and dispatched only by Speed Post, expressly barring over-the-counter handover, specifically to discourage repeated applicant visits to the Head Office.
A non-agricultural land certificate from the Circle Officer is specifically insisted upon for brick kilns and stone crushers where the land is classified as agricultural.

Quantitative data such as number of CTE and CTO applications received, disposed and pending by category for the required financial years still needs to be obtained from the Board for the CoR computation.

gaps.text: Quantitative throughput data (applications received/disposed/pending by category and year) was not provided by the Board and is needed for the CoR computation.

No specific turnaround time is given for laboratory analysis of effluent/stack/ambient air samples performed as part of CTE site verification, even though this step is described as a major driver of delay.

Internal file-movement discipline caps Regional Head file retention at 5 working days and order preparation at 5 working days, converting the overall service timeline into individually accountable internal steps.

Proposed single integrated consent (CTE-cum-CTO) with one application, one fee, one inspection and one order for Green/Orange non-EIA units, activated on filing of a commissioning-cum-performance report.

The exact process and turnaround for obtaining the Bank Guarantee (twice the consent fee) required for CTO auto-renewal — a physical instrument from a bank — is flagged as an offline step but no time estimate is given.

The document states Zonal/Head Office issue auto-renewal orders within 3 working days of receipt but does not clarify whether this 3-day step applies to fresh CTE issuance as well or only to the auto-renewal route.

The Board's own Guidelines separately state CTO must be processed within 120 days overall.
timeline.text: Same ARTPS-notified category slabs as CTE apply to CTO: 30 working days for Green up to 120 working days for Red category projects covered under the EIA Notification, 2006, with an internal 120-day statutory outer limit.

documents: Proposed steps to comply with the conditions stipulated in the Environmental Clearance (EC), where applicable
Consent fee paid online, based on the capital investment of the project as per the latest notification
Point-wise, evidence-based compliance report of the previous CTE/CTO, including production details
CA certificate on updated capital investment in land, building, plant and machinery without depreciation, as on date/end of financial year
Effluent analysis report (Water Act) and source emission plus ambient air quality monitoring reports (Air Act)
Details of water/air pollution control devices and solid & hazardous waste management facilities actually provided, as listed on the Board's website
Latest cess return/payment statement
Copy of the EC or other permission for first CTO, where applicable
licenses.documentsNote: CTO renewal / auto-renewal additionally requires: prescribed consent fee paid online; latest CA-certified financial balance sheet showing fixed assets; copy of the previous valid CTO and the latest environmental monitoring report; self-certification of compliance with existing consent conditions and Board directions; and a Bank Guarantee equal to twice the consent fee.

deemedApproval.text: There is no operational deemed-approval mechanism for CTO in Assam. The ARTPS Act provides a first and second appeal with compensatory cost against delay, but not automatic grant of the service.

validity.text: Validity adopted in line with CPCB direction on revised categorisation: Red 5 years, Orange 10 years, Green 15 years, subject to the number of years' fee actually paid. White category industries are exempt from consent and so no CTO/renewal applies to them. Auto-renewed CTOs are issued for a maximum of 5 years.

fees.text: Fee is structured on total capital investment (land, building, plant and machinery), not pollution load, with a separate consent fee payable under the Water Act and under the Air Act for CTO. An application form fee of Rs. 100 applies, over and above the consent fee. Specific CTO consent-fee slab amounts are not given in this document.

steps.title: Apply after the unit is constructed and pollution control systems installed, but before commencement of commercial production
Online payment of the consent fee separately under the Water Act and the Air Act
Upload point-wise compliance report of CTE conditions, CA certificate of capital investment, and effluent/stack/ambient air analysis reports from a recognised laboratory
Scrutiny by RO with mandatory site inspection and sampling to verify ETP/APCDs and waste-management facilities are installed and functional; inspection report uploaded
Processing at RO → Zonal Office → Head Office per delegation based on category/investment; TAC scrutiny for EIA/Red cases
Grant of CTO uploaded on OCMMS, validity 5/10/15 years for Red/Orange/Green respectively, subject to years' fee paid

licenses.issuingAuthority: State Fire Service, Assam — Designated Public Servant (DPS) at the district fire office (e.g. Kamrup Metro for Guwahati) for recommendation and compliance inspection; Directorate at Panbazar, Guwahati for final issue of the NOC / Fire Safety Certificate (Form G)

portal.name: Assam EoDB (Single Window) portal / Sewa Setu

timeline.basis: ARTPS Act notified timeline (Sewa Setu): 28 days from submission of a complete application. Department Citizen Charter separately commits to NOC issuance within 7 working days after a satisfactory inspection report.
timeline.text: Notified timeline is 28 days from a complete application, while the department's own Citizen Charter commits to 7 working days after a satisfactory inspection. In practice the stage from compliance report to NOC takes about 1 to 3 weeks in most cases, with cases of nearly 2 months seen where re-inspection or queries are involved; time spent replying to queries is not counted against the notified timeline. The overall time from first application to NOC is longer still, since the applicant needs time to install fire-fighting systems after the recommendation — a few weeks for small buildings, several months for large ones.

documents: Online application in the relevant standard form (Form I to X) with building details – height, number of floors, floor-wise use, built-up area, width of approach road, open spaces, staircases, lifts, water tank capacity and fire-fighting arrangements
Site plan, layout plan, service plan showing fire-fighting installations, and elevation/section plan for proposed or multi-storied buildings
For existing buildings: copy of building permission (GMC/GMDA) or trade licence
Land/ownership document or rent agreement, where applicable
Compliance Report in Form XI (at final stage)
For storage of gas, petroleum, chemicals or explosives: licence/permission from the concerned authority, quantity to be stored, and details of staff trained in basic fire fighting

deemedApproval.text: No deemed approval exists for the final Fire NOC — it certifies life safety and needs a physical check of installed systems, and fire clearance is specifically kept outside the time-limit/deemed-approval provision of the Assam MSME (Facilitation of Establishment and Operation) Act, 2020 (amended 2021). A limited scope exists only at the recommendation stage for low-hazard buildings below 15 m with drawings certified by an empanelled architect/auditor, where the recommendation may be treated as issued if the DPS does not act within the notified time.

validity.text: Validity depends on hazard category per Govt. OM of June 2022: Low hazard 3 years, Moderate hazard 2 years, High hazard 1 year, printed as a valid-up-to date on the certificate. The NOC remains valid only if there is no change in use, structure or fire-fighting arrangements; any such change needs a fresh NOC. Renewal is applied for in Form XII before expiry; if expired, the applicant must apply afresh through the full process. Renewal of Fire NOC was removed effective 25/12/2025: licences expiring before that date must apply afresh, while those expiring on or after 25/12/2025 do not require renewal and are deemed approved.

fees.text: The service was earlier free of cost; a fee was introduced on the EoDB portal in 2024 for Fire Safety Recommendation, NOC, temporary structures and Fire Attendance Certificate. Fee is paid online at two points — recommendation stage and compliance report/NOC stage — with applicants who already obtained a recommendation in or after 2016 exempted from the recommendation fee. Specific rupee amounts are not given in this document. Actual cost to the applicant is much higher than the statutory fee, driven mainly by drawings, consultant charges and fire-fighting equipment.

steps.title: Register on Assam EoDB portal/Sewa Setu and select the correct form by use of premises (Form I, III, V, or II/VII–X)
Fill online form, upload site/layout/service/elevation plans, pay prescribed fee online
Application goes to the Designated Public Servant (DPS); DPS checks drawings and inspects the site
DPS uploads Fire Safety Recommendation listing required fire safety measures per NBC 2016 Part 4
Applicant installs recommended measures and submits Compliance Report (Form XI) along with the NOC fee
DPS carries out compliance inspection; rectification notice and re-inspection if gaps are found
On satisfactory report, file goes to the Directorate at Panbazar; NOC/Fire Safety Certificate (Form G) issued online with hazard category and validity

remarks: Information is not consistent across platforms: Sewa Setu and the department website still show older details (e.g. free of cost), while the EoDB portal now collects a fee.

Renewal of Fire NOC has been removed effective from 25/12/2025: licences expiring before that date must apply afresh, while licences expiring on or after that date do not require renewal and are treated as deemed approval.
Many small establishments do not know whether they need a NOC; a simple public list of who needs one, by use, height and area, is needed.

findings.text: Information is inconsistent across platforms: Sewa Setu and the department website still show the service as free of cost, while the EoDB portal now collects a fee.
Small applicants (shops, PGs, small hostels, clinics) generally need to hire consultants or fire equipment vendors, as choosing the right form and uploading drawings is not easy for them.

The compliance-report-to-NOC stage typically takes 1 to 3 weeks but can take nearly 2 months when re-inspection or queries are involved, well beyond the department's own 7-working-day citizen charter commitment.
Time spent replying to queries, mostly on drawings, is not counted against the notified timeline, so the time felt by applicants is greater than the stated timeline.
Drawings already approved by GMDA/GMC for building permission are submitted again to the fire department, as the two systems do not share data, causing re-preparation of drawings and mismatches.
Separate forms (I to X) by activity leave applicants unsure which form to use for mixed-use buildings (shops + godown + hall), and they sometimes file more than once.
Other offices (trade licence, banks, insurance, education/health registrations) still ask for hard copies even though the NOC is online and verifiable through its token link.

There is no deemed approval for Fire NOC; the Assam MSME (Facilitation of Establishment and Operation) Act, 2020 (amended 2021) specifically keeps fire clearance outside the time-limit/deemed-approval provision.

A limited deemed-approval scope exists only at the recommendation stage for low-hazard buildings below 15 m with drawings certified by an empanelled architect/fire safety auditor, if the DPS does not act within the notified time; the final NOC should still follow inspection.
Open-space, setback and road-width norms cannot be met by many old buildings in congested areas such as Fancy Bazar, Paltan Bazar, Athgaon and Machkhowa.
Residential buildings converted into home stays, PGs, coaching centres or clinics cannot get a NOC because building permission does not match actual use.
The actual cost to the applicant is much higher than the statutory fee — drawings, consultant charges and fire-fighting equipment form the major part.
Inspection dates are fixed informally over phone, and applicants have to wait, rather than through a formal online slot-booking system.

Hazard classification is not always uniform: schools in Guwahati have been placed in Low hazard (3 years) in some cases and High hazard (1 year) in others, with no published occupancy-wise list to reduce discretion.
Suggested reform: combine the recommendation and compliance inspections into one for low-hazard buildings below 15 m where drawings are certified by an empanelled architect/auditor.
Suggested reform: integrate the fire portal with the GMDA/GMC building permission system so drawings are shared and buildings needing fire clearance are referred automatically.

Suggested reform: notify an alternative compliance package / retrofit standard (detection, alarm, extra extinguishers, sprinklers where possible) for existing buildings in congested old areas that cannot meet current open-space and road-width norms.
The NOC is issued fully online through EoDB with a computer-generated certificate verifiable by token/link — no office visit is needed for collection, and fake certificates are easy to detect.
Risk-based validity (3/2/1 years by hazard category) introduced in 2022 has reduced the number of renewals needed for low-hazard premises.

Renewal of Fire NOC was removed effective 25/12/2025; licences that expire before that date must apply afresh, while licences expiring on or after that date do not require renewal and are deemed approved.

gaps.text: Exact Fire NOC fee amounts (recommendation fee, NOC fee, temporary structure fee, Fire Attendance Certificate fee) introduced in 2024 are not given; the document only says rates follow a notified fee structure.

The document gives two different figures for the same overall timeline: the ARTPS/Sewa Setu notified timeline of 28 days from a complete application, versus the department Citizen Charter's own commitment of 7 working days after a satisfactory inspection report, without clarifying how the two relate.
No published list of which hazard category a given occupancy type falls into exists; the expert notes schools have been classified inconsistently as Low or High hazard without a stated reason.
Computer-generated Fire NOC verifiable via a token/link printed on the certificate, eliminating the need for an office visit to collect it and making fake certificates easy to detect.

Suggested joint GMC/GMDA–Fire single window for change-of-use cases (e.g. residential buildings converted to homestay/PG/clinic) that currently cannot obtain a Fire NOC because building permission does not match actual use.

The precise mechanics of the 25/12/2025 removal of Fire NOC renewal — specifically what 'deemed approval' requires of a holder whose NOC expires on or after that date — is stated only briefly and not elaborated.

licenses.issuingAuthority: Office of the Controller of Legal Metrology, Government of Assam — approval by the Controller (or an officer authorised by him); applications routed via the Assistant Controller/Inspector of Legal Metrology at district level

portal.name: Assam single-window portal for Legal Metrology

timeline.basis: ARTPS Act notified timelines on Sewa Setu: 15 working days for manufacturer (LM-1) and dealer (LD-1) licences and for registration of manufacturer/packer of pre-packed commodities (Form-I); 7 working days for verification and stamping of a new weighbridge (Form-6) and of new petrol/diesel dispensing pumps (Form-5). The department's Citizen Charter separately commits to 1–12 hours for routine verification of smaller weights/measures and 1–7 days for calibration of storage tanks.
timeline.text: Licensing and registration (manufacturer, dealer, repairer, pre-packed commodities) carry a 15-working-day notified timeline; verification/stamping of new weighbridges and petrol/diesel pumps carry a 7-working-day timeline, while the Citizen Charter commits routine verification of smaller instruments to 1–12 hours from presentation. These limits count only from a complete application, so time spent answering queries is not counted and effectively restarts the clock; the real wait for licences and in-situ verification depends on officer availability and tour programme.

documents: Dealer licence (LD-1): Valid trade licence from the Municipal Corporation/Board/Town Committee/Gaon Panchayat
Dealer licence (LD-1): VAT/Sales Tax registration number, or CST number, or Professional Tax registration number, or IT number
Dealer licence (LD-1): Model approval certificate issued by the Government of India for the instruments to be sold
Dealer licence (LD-1): Authorisation letter from the manufacturer allowing the dealer to sell that weight or measure

Manufacturer licence (LM-1) / Repairer licence (LR-1): Trade licence, tax registration number, model approval certificate, proof of premises, and details of workshop, tools and skilled workers; manufacturer must also show working standards and testing equipment held
Registration of Manufacturer/Packer of pre-packed commodities (Form-I): Trade licence from the Municipal Corporation/Board/Town Committee/village panchayat
Registration (Form-I): VAT/Sales Tax/CST/Professional Tax/IT number
Registration (Form-I): Partnership deed, if a partnership firm
Registration (Form-I): Factory registration certificate
Registration (Form-I): Address proof
Registration (Form-2, importer): Importer certificate issued by the Ministry of Commerce, Government of India
Verification of new weighbridge (Form-6): Model approval certificate of the weighbridge issued by the Government of India
Verification of new weighbridge (Form-6): Purchase invoice of the weighbridge
Verification of new weighbridge (Form-6): Purchase invoice of one tonne of test weight
Verification of new weighbridge (Form-6): No Objection Certificate from the Civil Administration/Municipality/Board/Town Committee/village panchayat
Verification of new petrol/diesel dispensing pumps (Form-5): Letter addressed to the Controller from the oil company concerned
Verification of new petrol/diesel dispensing pumps (Form-5): Model approval certificate of the dispensing pump issued by the Government of India
licenses.documentsNote: This ED covers three distinct sub-services bundled under Legal Metrology: (A) licences for Manufacturer/Dealer/Repairer of weights and measures, (B) registration of Manufacturer/Packer/Importer of pre-packed commodities (LMPC), and (C) verification and stamping (and re-verification) of weights and measures. Documents above are grouped and labelled by sub-service as described in the ED.

deemedApproval.text: No deemed approval exists for any Legal Metrology service in Assam. Crossing the 15-day or 7-day timeline only gives the applicant the ARTPS Act appeal route, which provides a decision and compensation for delay but not automatic grant. The Assam Ease of Doing Business Act, 2016 deemed-approval machinery does not cover these services since they are granted under the Central Legal Metrology Act, 2009, and neither that Act nor the State Rules contain a deemed-grant provision of their own.

validity.text: Licences (Manufacturer/Dealer/Repairer) are valid for a minimum of one calendar year and may be renewed by the Controller for one to five years at a time; because the portal fee is charged per year, most small traders take a one-year licence and renew annually (Form LM-2/LD-2/LR-2 before expiry; late renewal allowed within three months of expiry on payment of an additional fee, after which a fresh licence is needed). Registration as Manufacturer/Packer/Importer of pre-packed commodities under Rule 27 is a one-time registration with no annual renewal (Rs. 100 fee for any later change). Verification stamps last 24 months for weights, capacity/length measures, tape, beam scale and counter machines; 60 months for storage tanks; and 12 months for all other instruments including weighbridges, fuel dispensing pumps and tank lorries — the stamp period is cut short and re-verification required if the machine is shifted or repaired, even before the period ends.

fees.text: Licence/registration fees shown on the Assam portal: Manufacturer licence (LM-1) Rs. 2,000/year; Dealer licence (LD-1) Rs. 500/year; Repairer licence (LR-1) not fixed; pre-packed commodity registration (Form-I) Rs. 500, with Rs. 100 for any later change; appeal fees Rs. 200 to the Controller and Rs. 500 to the State Government. Separately, verification/stamping fees are fixed per instrument by type and denomination under the Schedule to the Assam Legal Metrology (Enforcement) Rules, 2011, ranging from a few rupees for a small weight to a few thousand rupees for a weighbridge, with an extra charge for first-time verification, a further charge plus travel expenses for in-situ verification at the trader's premises, and an additional fee per quarter of delay for late re-verification; the online Form-5/Form-6 pages show the fee as N/A since it is worked out at the time of the test and deposited in the treasury head, often by challan.

steps.title: Business decides which licence it needs — LM-1 (manufacturer), LD-1 (dealer) or LR-1 (repairer)
Register and log in on the Assam single-window Legal Metrology portal (metrology.eodbassam.in) or via Sewa Setu
Fill the form online, upload required documents, pay the licence fee online
System generates acknowledgement with application reference number; SMS and e-mail sent
Application goes to the Assistant Controller/Inspector of Legal Metrology of that district for document checking
Legal Metrology Officer visits premises to verify workshop, equipment and stock match the application
File goes to the Controller of Legal Metrology (or an authorised officer) for approval
Licence issued; applicant gets SMS and e-mail and downloads the licence from the portal
Renewal done in Form LM-2/LD-2/LR-2 before the licence expires
Registration (LMPC): apply under Rule 27 of the Packaged Commodities Rules, 2011 — Form-I for manufacturer/packer, Form-2 for importer
Online application on the same portal, with documents and fee
Legal Metrology Officer checks the papers and the label declarations
Registration certificate issued and downloadable from the portal
No weight or measure can be sold or used in trade until it is verified and stamped by a Legal Metrology Officer
For small items, user brings the instrument to the office/camp; for fixed machines (weighbridge, petrol pump, storage tank) the officer visits the site
For a new weighbridge, apply in Form-6; for new petrol/diesel pumps, apply in Form-5, with the model approval certificate
Officer tests the instrument against standard weights and measures; if off, trader gets it adjusted/repaired and it is tested again
If correct, officer stamps the instrument and issues a verification certificate; fee paid and deposited into the treasury head
Re-verification required when the stamp period ends — trader must apply again and go through the same test
Re-verification required if a machine is shifted to a new place or repaired, even if the stamp has not expired

ed.location: Office of the Controller of Legal Metrology, Assam, R.K. Mission Road, Ulubari, Guwahati, Kamrup – 781007
ed.expert: Shri Baben Das; Shri Pranjal Das

remarks: These services are granted under the Legal Metrology Act, 2009 (a Central Act); the Assam Ease of Doing Business Act, 2016 applies only to clearances under State laws, so its deemed-approval machinery does not cover Legal Metrology services — this is the stated legal reason deemed approval has not been introduced here.

The biggest recurring cost in this service is not the fee itself but the recurring burden — annual re-verification of every machine, business lost while a weighbridge/pump is shut for testing, and time spent arranging the officer's visit; the CoR model for this service should be built around number of instruments and frequency of verification, not number of licences.

The department's own forms (LM-1, LD-1, LR-1, Form-I, Form-2) remain published on the website as downloadable PDFs to be submitted in person to the Assistant Controller/Inspector, alongside the online route, which confuses applicants.

findings.text: There is no online way to fix the officer's visit for in-situ verification; the trader has to chase the officer by phone or in person, described as the single biggest cause of both delay and unofficial payments in this service.

Documents the Government already holds — trade licence, VAT/Sales Tax/CST/Professional Tax/IT number, factory registration certificate, partnership deed, address proof — are asked for again at Legal Metrology licensing/registration.
The same documents are asked for again at renewal, even when nothing about the business has changed.
The law allows a licence for up to five years, but the portal fee is charged per year, so most traders take a one-year licence and come back every year.
There is overlap between the trade licence (already checked by the local body for the same premises and business) and the Legal Metrology licence, which repeats the premises/identity checking.
The trader must buy and keep one tonne of test weight for a weighbridge — a real capital cost for a small operator — which sits idle for the rest of the year.
Each district has very few Legal Metrology officers, and the same officer handles verification, enforcement, inspections and court cases, so verification gets delayed.
Annual re-verification of most machines is required because the stamp period for most instruments is 12 months, even though most instruments pass the test every time.
There is no deemed approval for any Legal Metrology service; the appeal route under the ARTPS Act gives a decision and compensation for delay but not automatic grant of the licence or registration.

Licences and registrations are granted under the Central Legal Metrology Act, 2009, so the deemed-approval machinery of the State EODB Act does not cover them — this is given as the main legal reason deemed approval has not been introduced.
The verification fee is shown as N/A on the online Form-5/Form-6 service pages, since it is worked out instrument-by-instrument at the time of testing and deposited in the treasury head.
The department's own forms (LM-1, LD-1, LR-1, Form-I, Form-2) remain published as downloadable PDFs for in-person submission alongside the online route, which confuses applicants.

Suggested reform: online slot booking for verification/re-verification on the portal, with a guaranteed visit within 7 working days, SMS confirmation of the date, and auto-escalation to the Assistant Controller if the visit does not happen.
Suggested reform: allow accredited third-party verification agencies for low-risk instruments, with the department doing audit checks and keeping full enforcement powers.
Suggested reform: move good-record, low-risk instruments to a 24-month re-verification cycle while keeping 12 months for petrol pumps, weighbridges, bullion scales and tank lorries.
Suggested reform: a discounted five-year composite licence fee plus auto-renewal on self-declaration for traders with no pending case, replacing yearly paperwork for an unchanged business.

The Citizen Charter gives realistic, honest time standards for verification (e.g. 1 to 12 hours from presentation by the user, depending on the machine and any repair needed) rather than a padded number of days.
All main services are listed on Sewa Setu under the ARTPS Act with timeline, document checklist and fee published in advance, plus a right of appeal if the timeline is missed.
A single, clearly stated treasury head is used for all fee deposits, making the money trail easy to follow and audit.

The CoR model for this service should be built around the number of instruments and frequency of verification rather than number of licences, since the recurring verification burden, not the fee, is the biggest cost to traders.

gaps.text: Repairer licence (Form LR-1) fee is stated as not fixed, with no further detail on how it is actually determined or what range applies.

No figure is given for the typical waiting time for an in-situ verification visit (weighbridge/pump/tank); the document only says it depends on the officer's tour programme, with a 30-day advance-notice requirement on the trader's side.

Separate online services exist for the two highest-value instruments — new weighbridges (Form-6) and new petrol/diesel dispensing pumps (Form-5) — each with a short 7-working-day timeline and its own checklist, rather than lumping them into one general verification service.
Recommended: allow only one consolidated query per application, raised within 7 working days, with the clock not restarting after that, so the notified 15-day and 7-day timelines actually hold.

No figure is given for how many Legal Metrology officers actually serve each district — only that there are very few who also handle enforcement and court work — which would ground the capacity-constraint finding with a specific number.

The Checklist Required section states a repairer must get every repaired instrument re-verified and stamped before it goes back into use, but does not state a maximum time allowed for that re-verification turnaround.
